name: Backhand topspin
summary: A spinny backhand driven by forearm and wrist from in front of the body.
whenToUse: To open against a long push to your backhand, or to keep topspin pressure in a backhand rally.

keyPoints.stance: Square or right foot slightly forward (left foot if left-handed), knees well bent.
keyPoints.bodyAction: Small upward push from the legs; the upper body stays in front of the ball.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Short to medium: from below the ball, finishing at about eye level.
keyPoints.timing: Top of the bounce against topspin; at or just after the top against backspin.
keyPoints.tablePosition: Close to mid-distance, ball in front of the body.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow forward and a little up. Wrist cocks back, then whips up and forward through the ball.
keyPoints.recovery: Bat back in front of the body.
keyPoints.anticipation: Against backspin lift more; against topspin close the bat and go forward.

cues: Elbow forward, bat below the ball

learningPath.task: Watch from the front: see the wrist cock back before contact.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along: drop the bat, cock the wrist, whip up and forward.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Did the wrist cock back first?
Did the bat finish at eye level?

learningPath.task: Slow backspin to the backhand, one at a time.
Backhand topspin rally against a block.
Open with the backhand, then switch to the forehand.
Open-up game: open with the backhand when the ball is long.

gamePatterns.situation: A long push to your backhand.
gamePatterns.how: Open with a spinny backhand topspin to their backhand, then expect a block.
Topspin cross-court, then change down the line when they step over.

fixes: Open the face a little and brush up
Close the bat and go forward
Move so the ball is in front

penholdNotes: Modern penholders play this on the reverse side with a similar wrist action.
